claim: Postoperative knee instability is one of the major reasons accounting for unsatisfactory outcomes after TKA.
source: Postoperative knee instability is one of the major reasons accounting for unsatisfactory outcomes, as well as a major failure mechanism leading to total knee arthroplasty (TKA) revision.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and introduction as established knowledge in the field.

claim: Postoperative knee instability is a major failure mechanism leading to TKA revision.
source: Postoperative knee instability is one of the major reasons accounting for unsatisfactory outcomes, as well as a major failure mechanism leading to total knee arthroplasty (TKA) revision.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the field.

claim: Subjective knee instability is not well defined clinically.
source: Nevertheless, subjective knee instability is not well defined clinically, plausibly because the relationships between instability and implant kinematics during functional activities of daily living remain unclear.
evidence: This is stated as a gap in current clinical understanding.

claim: The relationships between instability and implant kinematics during functional activities of daily living remain unclear.
source: Nevertheless, subjective knee instability is not well defined clinically, plausibly because the relationships between instability and implant kinematics during functional activities of daily living remain unclear.
evidence: This is stated as a gap in current knowledge.

claim: The influence of joint instability on muscle synergy patterns is poorly understood.
source: Although muscles play a critical role in supporting the dynamic stability of the knee joint, the influence of joint instability on muscle synergy patterns is poorly understood.
evidence: This is stated as a gap in current understanding.

claim: Average condylar A-P translations were comparable between stable and unstable TKA groups.
source: Our results reveal that average condylar A-P translations, rotations, as well as their ranges of motion were comparable between stable and unstable groups.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study's experimental data.

claim: Average condylar rotations were comparable between stable and unstable TKA groups.
source: Our results reveal that average condylar A-P translations, rotations, as well as their ranges of motion were comparable between stable and unstable groups.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study's experimental data.

claim: Ranges of motion of condylar A-P translations and rotations were comparable between stable and unstable TKA groups.
source: Our results reveal that average condylar A-P translations, rotations, as well as their ranges of motion were comparable between stable and unstable groups.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study's experimental data.

claim: The unstable group exhibited more heterogeneous muscle synergy patterns compared to the stable group.
source: However, the unstable group exhibited more heterogeneous muscle synergy patterns and prolonged activation of knee flexors compared to the stable group.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study's EMG data analysis.

claim: The unstable group exhibited prolonged activation of knee flexors compared to the stable group.
source: However, the unstable group exhibited more heterogeneous muscle synergy patterns and prolonged activation of knee flexors compared to the stable group.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study's EMG data analysis.

claim: Subjects who reported instability events during measurement showed distinct, subject-specific tibiofemoral kinematic patterns in the early/mid-swing phase of gait.
source: In addition, subjects who reported instability events during measurement showed distinct, subject-specific tibiofemoral kinematic patterns in the early/mid-swing phase of gait.
evidence: This is a finding from the study's kinematic analysis of specific subjects.

claim: Accurate movement analysis is sensitive for detecting acute instability events.
source: Our findings suggest that accurate movement analysis is sensitive for detecting acute instability events, but might be less robust in identifying general joint instability.

claim: Accurate movement analysis might be less robust in identifying general joint instability.
source: Our findings suggest that accurate movement analysis is sensitive for detecting acute instability events, but might be less robust in identifying general joint instability.

claim: Muscle synergy patterns can identify muscular adaptation associated with underlying chronic knee instability.
source: Conversely, muscle synergy patterns seem to be able to identify muscular adaptation associated with underlying chronic knee instability.

claim: Postoperative knee instability accounts for up to 26% of TKA revisions.
source: Knee instability is one of the most common reasons for unsatisfactory outcomes after TKA, accounting for up to 26% of revisions (Parratte and Pagnano, 2008; Wilson et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Inadequate soft-tissue balancing is associated with knee instability after TKA.
source: This lack of understanding is likely due to the multitude of factors that are associated with knee instability, including inadequate soft-tissue balancing (Hosseini Nasab et al., 2019; Song et al., 2014), loss of ligamentous integrity (Nagle and Glynn, 2020), and improper component sizing (Nagle and Glynn, 2020; Parratte and Pagnano, 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Loss of ligamentous integrity is associated with knee instability after TKA.
source: This lack of understanding is likely due to the multitude of factors that are associated with knee instability, including inadequate soft-tissue balancing (Hosseini Nasab et al., 2019; Song et al., 2014), loss of ligamentous integrity (Nagle and Glynn, 2020), and improper component sizing (Nagle and Glynn, 2020; Parratte and Pagnano, 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Clinical assessments of knee instability are highly subjective with large inter-rater variability.

claim: Passive knee laxity plays a key role for functional outcomes after TKA.
source: Studies using these techniques have demonstrated that passive knee laxity plays a key role for functional outcomes and patient satisfaction after TKA (Oh et al., 2015; Jones et al., 2006).

claim: Downhill walking is considered a challenging task for subjects with knee pathologies.
source: Specifically, both downhill walking and stair descent are considered as challenging tasks for subjects with knee pathologies (Stacoff et al., 2005; Simon et al., 2018), and could therefore present relevant activities for provoking feelings of instability.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Muscular deficits are often observed after TKA.

claim: Muscular deficits after TKA closely correlate with physical impairment and limitations in daily activities.

claim: Increased knee extensor and flexor co-activation is observed in the early postoperative phase after TKA.
source: Here, adaptation of muscle recruitment patterns in the early postoperative phase, where increased knee extensor (quadriceps) and flexor (hamstrings) co-activation has generally been observed, is thought to enhance knee stability (Lundberg et al., 2016; Benedetti et al., 2003).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Increased knee extensor and flexor co-activation is thought to enhance knee stability after TKA.

claim: In total, 17 subjects with 18 replaced knees were recruited for the study.
source: In total, 17 subjects (age ≥45 years, pain VAS ≤3) with 18 replaced knees implanted with Persona cruciate retaining (CR) TKA components and an ultra-congruent (UC) inlay (Zimmer Biomet, Warsaw, IN, USA) were recruited at least 1 year postoperatively.
evidence: This describes the study cohort.

claim: All recruited subjects were at least 1 year postoperatively.
source: In total, 17 subjects (age ≥45 years, pain VAS ≤3) with 18 replaced knees implanted with Persona cruciate retaining (CR) TKA components and an ultra-congruent (UC) inlay (Zimmer Biomet, Warsaw, IN, USA) were recruited at least 1 year postoperatively.

claim: Both cruciate ligaments were sacrificed in all TKA knees in the study.
source: Both cruciate ligaments were sacrificed in all TKA knees.

claim: Eight TKA knees were recruited into the unstable cohort from subjects reporting episodes of buckling, shifting, or giving away of the operated knee during daily activities in the 3 months prior to recruitment.
source: Of the 18, 8 TKA knees (3M:5F, 68.9 ± 8.3 years, 31.9 ± 20.4 months postoperatively, body mass index [BMI] 26.1 ± 3.2 kg/m2) were recruited from subjects reporting episodes of buckling, shifting, or giving away of the operated knee during daily activities in the 3 months prior to recruitment, with or without clinical signs of instability (unstable cohort).
evidence: This describes the unstable cohort recruitment criteria.

claim: Ten TKA knees were recruited into the stable group from subjects with no sensation of instability in the operated knee in the 3-month period prior to recruitment.
source: Ten TKA knees were recruited into the stable group (7M:3F, 62.6 ± 6.8 years, 33.9 ± 8.5 months postoperatively, BMI 29.4 ± 4.8 kg/m2) from subjects with no sensation of instability in the operated knee in the same 3-month period prior to recruitment.
evidence: This describes the stable cohort recruitment criteria.

claim: One stable knee showed signs of mild hyperextension.
